verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit's own auto-review configuration (reviews.auto_review) covers each part of the story: skipping draft PRs, limiting reviews to certain branches, re-enabling by keyword or label, and pausing after a set number of commits. On-demand triggering is documented through @coderabbitai review, full review, pause, resume and ignore commands. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that these triggers and filters work as documented.

support.subject: As a developer, I control when reviews run — skip drafts, trigger on demand, filter by branch or label — so the bot shows up only when wanted

citations.quote: you can disable reviews globally and re-enable them by keyword or label, apply them only to certain branches, skip draft PRs, and pause after a set number of commits
Configure when and how CodeRabbit automatically reviews pull requests using the `reviews.auto_review` settings.
Use @coderabbitai full review when you want a complete pass over the entire pull request.
Pause, resume, ignore reviews, request manual reviews, resolve comments, request approval, and update pull request summaries using @coderabbitai commands.
